title: CS ask journey stitch and implementation notes
content:
TL;DR: stitched together ~40 recent customer asks into a journey-centric view (onboarding -> integration -> production ops -> billing). Identified 6 high-leverage short fixes, 3 medium-term implementation sketches, and open questions to validate with 3 top customers. This doc is intentionally rough — mix of customer quotes, quick acceptance checks, and suggested owners.

Context and approach:
- Why a journey stitch: many requests are duplicate across touchpoints but expressed differently (e.g., 'slow cold-start' vs 'latency spikes on first call'). Organizing by journey gives clearer solution surface and reduces rework.
- Data sources: CS logs (May-Sep 2026), three on-record account calls (ACME, Finova, EduLabs), Slack threads, last 30 days of support tickets.
- Method: tag each ask with journey stage, severity (S1–S3), frequency bucket (1–5) and suggested complexity (quick/med/large).

Journey map highlights (most frequent pain points):
1) Onboarding (API key, model selection, getting started)
  - Signal: new teams repeatedly ask for a sample 'production profile' for common use cases (chat, summarization, embeddings).
  - Top requests: example rate-limit settings, pre-baked config templates, clearer model variant table.
  - Customer quote: "We want a one-click template for a small chat agent — which model, what batch size, what timeout?" (Finova)

2) Integration (SDKs, retries, error semantics)
  - Signal: SDK inconsistencies and unclear retry semantics surface in integration work for ~15% of tickets.
  - Top requests: deterministic retry guidance, SDK update notes with breaking changes flagged, sample code for streaming + tool-calls.
  - Quick idea: add a small "integration checklist" in SDK README and Console route pages.

3) Production ops (latency, fallbacks, autoscaling)
  - Signal: customers want clearer guidance on when to use Dedicated vs Hosted and how fallbacks behave under load.
  - Top requests: latency SLO playbook, a visualization of fallback routing, and a canned canary rollout policy for models.
  - Notable pattern: several customers experienced higher tail latency during periodic batch jobs; likely mis-configured batching windows.

4) Observability & debugging (traces, token cost attribution)
  - Signal: hard to tie token cost regressions to specific prompts/rollouts.
  - Top requests: token-attribution breakdown per request id, automatic alert when cost per session > baseline, and per-model quality regression hooks.

5) Billing & quotas
  - Signal: confusion around burst credits and quota resets; customers want predictable alerts before throttles.
  - Top requests: email + webhook quota threshold alerts, clearer billing examples for embeddings-heavy workloads.

Short fixes (low effort, high signal) — 6 proposals:
1) Console: add "starter profiles" dropdown on new-route creation (chat, summarization, embed) with pre-populated config (model, batch, timeout). Complexity: quick. Owner: product-hosted-api. Acceptance: one-click creates route with recommended settings; docs link.

2) SDK README: canonical retry table and sample streaming+tool-call snippet. Complexity: quick. Owner: developer-experience. Acceptance: merge PR and add to release notes.

3) Quotas: implement webhook for quota thresholds (50/75/90%). Complexity: quick. Owner: platform-engineering. Acceptance: customers can subscribe a URL and receive JSON alerts during demo.

4) Support playbook: canned troubleshooting checklist for latency spikes (check batching window, KV cache warm-up, model variant mismatches). Complexity: quick. Owner: customer-success + eng-serving-runtime. Acceptance: distributed as KB article + checklist template used in 3 tickets.

5) Runbook snippet: recommended Dedicated vs Hosted decision tree for common volume tiers. Complexity: quick. Owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services. Acceptance: decision tree published in console help center.

6) Billing example sheet: create 3 sample billing scenarios (low token chat, embedding-first, high-concurrency) for public docs. Complexity: quick. Owner: finance-and-legal + product. Acceptance: published doc + link in pricing page.

Medium-term sketches (3 items; need eng design + ETA Q4 2026–Q1 2027):
A) Token-level attribution export (CSV/JSON) by request id and session; include model version, prompt hash, and token counts. Purpose: enable customers to map cost regressions to prompt changes. Risks: PII and token data retention rules; needs privacy review. Suggested next-step: scope minimal export fields and run privacy review with security. Owner: observability + security.

B) Canary rollout templates and automated fallback visualizer: a console UI that allows creating a canary (10% traffic to new model) with automatic fallback to previous variant and visible metrics. Scope: UI + backend routing policy + metrics instrumentation. Owner: product-console + serving-runtime.

C) Batching-windows diagnostics: instrument and surface per-route batching histograms (window sizes, wait times, avg tokens per batch). This will help SRE/CS troubleshoot intermittent tail latency. Owner: serving-runtime + observability.

Open questions / validation steps (to resolve before committing engineering hours):
- Which customers would pilot token attribution? Need 2–3 sign-ups; ask ACME, EduLabs, and Finova.
- Privacy: what token-level fields are acceptable? Is prompt-hash enough instead of raw prompt?
- Prioritization: rank short fixes vs medium items in roadmap — proposed: 6 quick fixes in next sprint, medium items Q4 roadmap backlog.

Suggested prioritization matrix (quick note):
- Short fix value x effort: (all high value / low effort) -> schedule in next 2 sprints.
- Medium sketches: high value / medium effort -> require scoping epics and aligned owners.

Acceptance criteria examples (for tickets created from above items):
- Starter profiles: route created + default config applied + clickthrough docs; tested with new account.
- Quota webhook: sends payload with route id, threshold level, timestamp; retry semantics documented.
- SDK README: includes snippet, table, and changelog entry; verified by two integrator customers.

Risk notes and tradeoffs:
- Token-level exports increase security/privacy burden and storage cost — need to estimate retention and access controls.
- Adding many console templates could increase cognitive load; prefer minimal curated set (3–4 starters).
- Batching visibility may surface internal infra variability; coordinate with SRE to avoid noisy dashboards.

Next steps (owner-level):
- Aisha: coordinate scoping call with product-hosted-api + devexp (week of Sep 21).
- Miguel: draft SDK README PR and assign to devexp reviewer by Sep 24.
- Emma: reach out to ACME and Finova for pilot interest on token attribution by Sep 28.
- Jonas: start a lightweight security intake for token export (due Oct 5).

Notes to self / raw snippets captured from calls (verbatim):
- "We iterate prompts weekly and then see a 3x token cost spike — no way to trace it back" — ACME.
- "If there was a pre-built small chat profile, we'd ship faster to pilot customers" — EduLabs.
- "Our SREs want the batching histogram before we can sign an SLA" — Finova infra lead.

Unresolved / follow-up items:
- Create a small survey (5 questions) to quantify frequency of each pain; target 25 customer responses.
- Build a short demo for quota webhook to show at next CS sync.

Appendix (quick mapping table sample, raw):
- Ask ID: CS-2026-189 | Stage: production ops | Frequency: 4 | Severity: S2 | Short fix candidate: support playbook.
- Ask ID: CS-2026-210 | Stage: onboarding | Frequency: 3 | Severity: S1 | Short fix candidate: starter profile.
- Ask ID: CS-2026-233 | Stage: observability | Frequency: 2 | Severity: S2 | Medium candidate: token attribution.

If helpful I can convert this into a small slide deck or a one-pager for exec review. For now, marking as draft while we validate pilots and privacy constraints.

-- Aisha
